title: The Unrestricted Ride: ZIPGO
body:
ZIPGO operates on a pay-per-minute rental model. Customers pay for a defined riding duration. Once the purchased time expires, the bicycle is expected to stop or safely restrict further use until the customer pays to continue.

However, ZIPGO bicycles continue operating after the paid duration has expired. A customer who purchases a ₹100 ride package may continue riding beyond the purchased time without a clear interruption. The company later applies an additional usage charge, for example ₹120 for the extra usage.

Customers argue that the bicycle should have clearly warned them or prevented further use once their paid time ended. They see the additional charge as unexpected and feel that the system puts them in a trap. Some customers respond by switching to competing rental services.

The business problem: ZIPGO's current system allows usage to continue after the paid duration expires, creating unexpected charges, customer dissatisfaction and a risk of losing repeat users.

Your challenge: rethink ZIPGO's rental and revenue model. Develop a solution that protects customers from unexpected charges while keeping the business financially sustainable.
• Technology: how should the bicycle respond when the paid riding duration expires?
• Pricing: should ZIPGO introduce alerts, a grace period, automatic extensions or a different pricing structure?
• Customer retention: how will ZIPGO prevent customers from switching to competitors?
• Revenue: how can the company charge fairly for additional usage without discouraging repeat rides?
• Financial viability: how can ZIPGO implement the solution across its fleet while controlling costs?

Final deliverable: a revised business model that improves pricing transparency, protects customer experience, retains users and maintains ZIPGO's profitability.
